gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the inverter inside a power station costs energy: named testers measured a 1,024 Wh unit (Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2) giving only 850–907 Wh at its AC outlets, and The Technology Man measured about 17 W of idle draw with AC switched on and nothing plugged in (20% of the battery gone in 12 hours).
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and cited no results, so there were no rival pages to compare against. Its answer has only a qualitative table (built-in battery, cost, best for) and says a power station 'already contains an inverter'. It gives no measured figure for how much a rated Wh number shrinks through that inverter, and none for the idle draw of leaving AC on. Those are the two costs a shopper choosing between a power station and an inverter on their own battery pays either way.
decides: It confirms the choice instead of flipping it, and it corrects how a shopper should size either option. Plan on about 83–89% of the rated Wh at the AC outlets: 850–910 Wh from a 1 kWh station, and about 210 Wh from the 245 Wh RIVER 3. If you only run DC loads (12 V fridge, USB), the DC outlets or a battery without an inverter avoid part of that loss. Switch AC off when it isn't in use, because a 17 W idle drains about 400 Wh a day. That is roughly 40% of a 1 kWh station. Among the 1 kWh candidates the measured AC yield is close: Jackery 1000 v2 910 Wh and DELTA 3 Plus 910 Wh vs C1000 Gen 2 850–907 Wh. Measured efficiency therefore doesn't separate them; charge speed and price will.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, constant 1 kW load
findings.source_title: Record Breaking Charge Speed: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man, Gidon)
findings.note: Constant 1 kW resistive heater load, measured with an energy-monitoring plug. It ran just over 54 minutes. Review dated 4 Nov 2025.

findings.label: Idle draw with AC output on, no load
findings.source_title: Record Breaking Charge Speed: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man, Gidon)
findings.note: 12-hour test with Smart AC Output Mode off. Charge fell from 100% to 80%: 0.2 × 1,024 Wh ≈ 205 Wh / 12 h ≈ 17 W. The reviewer calls this about average. Extrapolated to a day, that is about 410 Wh.

findings.label: Usable DC energy, 12 V at 8 A
findings.source_title: Record Breaking Charge Speed: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man, Gidon)
findings.note: DC load tester set to 8 A on the 12 V output.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, ~250 W load
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but... Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten)
findings.note: EU 230 V version. Continuous ~250 W load until shutdown at 1%. Fluctuating loads gave less (no figure). AC charging took 1,110 Wh in (~92%). Noise about 45 dB at 1 m under heavy load or fast charge. Published 21 Dec 2025, updated 5 Oct 2026.

findings.label: Measured power output (load bank)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey)
findings.note: Light-bar load bank. The page's spec table also shows 'usable capacity 80%' against a 1,056 Wh claim, which is inconsistent with its text, so I used the text figure. Measured AC charging averaged 1,097 Wh/hr; full in 56 min standard, 49 min UltraFast. Review dated 23 Jul 2026.

findings.label: Measured power output (load bank)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 Review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey)
findings.note: Same lab and method as the C1000 Gen 2 entry. A full recharge took almost 2 hours at a measured 563 Wh/hr. Review dated 23 Jul 2026.

findings.label: Usable energy, 100% to 0% discharge
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty)
findings.note: The load used is not stated. A recharge from 0 to 100% took 1,180 Wh (86.8%). Measured UPS transfer time was just over 8 ms (rated 10 ms). Review dated 2 Jan 2025.

findings.label: Usable energy, 300 W load
findings.note: Full discharge until shutdown, 300 W fan load (the unit's rated maximum). A recharge to 100% took 270 Wh from the wall. Peak AC charge draw was 322 W. 210/245 = 85.7%. Review dated 7 Oct 2024.
